You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Hijack after WriteHeader/Write corrupts the connection. Wrapped output is `"RAW\n"` with no status line or headers; plain net/http sends `"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-A: 1\r\n...RAW\n"`. Cause: `Hijack` forwards without committing the buffered status and headers, then `finish` writes to the hijacked conn. Fix: commit (and flush the buffer) in `Hijack` before forwarding, as `Flush` does.
- [blocking] Hijack with no write logs a spurious server message. The wrapper's `finish` calls `WriteHeader` on the hijacked conn, so the server logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...commit (etag.go:103)`. Plain net/http with the same handler logs nothing. Same fix as above (skip commit/finish once hijacked).
- [blocking] Headers changed after an explicit `WriteHeader(200)` take effect under ETag but not under plain net/http. Probe: handler does `WriteHeader(200)`, then `Header().Set("Content-Type","text/csv")`, then writes. Plain sends `text/plain; charset=utf-8`; wrapped sends `text/csv`. The `X-Late` header shows the same difference. Fix: snapshot the header map at `WriteHeader(200)` and restore it at commit.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: *` on a HEAD response with no body and no handler ETag returns 304 (`ifNoneMatchMatches` returns true before the ETag check). Defensible per RFC ("*" matches any 200), but a 304 with no validator is questionable. Reproduced; not a criterion violation.
- [minor] With `Compress` outer and `ETag` inner, gzip and identity responses share one ETag. Vary: Accept-Encoding covers caches, so this is not a correctness failure in the probes. Not an acceptance-criteria failure.
- [minor] Untracked `FEATURE_FLOW.md` at repo root is not part of the listed change. Not reviewed further.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [minor] Trailer values set after Write are dropped. The plain chunked response sends `X-Sum: abc` as a trailer, but the wrapped one does not, because finish sets Content-Length and restoreHeader wipes the late key. With an explicit Content-Length, plain net/http also drops the trailer, so the difference only comes from criterion 5. Not blocking.
- [minor] When the underlying writer's Hijack fails and the handler wrote nothing, `committed` is already true, so finish skips the ETag and 304 step. The body written afterwards is still delivered, but with no ETag. Reproduced with a fake Hijacker that returns an error.
- [minor] Generated ETag on GET 200 (including empty bodies and handler-set headers with no write) appears where plain net/http sends none. This is the intended behaviour, not a defect.
- [minor] Handler ETag set after WriteHeader(200) or after Write: plain sends no ETag and the wrapper generates one. A matching If-None-Match gives 200 in both, so the behaviour is consistent. Not blocking.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix three reproduced bugs in the new chi ETag middleware (repo /tmp/ff-eval-5q_zbnef/workspace) without changing any other behaviour.

FILES: middleware/etag.go (etagResponseWriter: WriteHeader/Write/Flush/Hijack/commit/finish), middleware/etag_test.go. Read both first.

CONSTRAINTS: Edit only those two files. Stdlib only. Keep all existing tests passing.

Bugs (each reproduced against plain net/http behind httptest.NewServer):
1. Hijack after WriteHeader/Write: the wrapped client gets the raw bytes with no status line or headers, while plain net/http sends `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nX-A: 1...` then the raw bytes. Fix: in Hijack, if a status is pending and nothing has been committed yet, commit the status, headers and buffered body to the underlying writer first (as Flush does, but without calling the underlying Flush), then forward Hijack. In every case mark the writer so `finish` does nothing afterwards.
2. Hijack with no write: `finish` calls WriteHeader on the hijacked conn, and the server logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection`. Same fix: after Hijack, finish must not touch the underlying writer.
3. Header changes made after an explicit or implicit WriteHeader(200) take effect under ETag but not under plain net/http (handler: WriteHeader(200); Header().Set("Content-Type","text/csv"); Header().Set("X-Late","1"); Write → plain sends sniffed text/plain and no X-Late; wrapped sends text/csv and X-Late). Fix: when the final status 200 is recorded (explicit WriteHeader(200) or the first Write), snapshot `Header().Clone()`. When committing that 200 (in Flush, Hijack or finish), first restore the live header map's contents to the snapshot (delete the keys, copy the snapshot back in), then apply the ETag, 304 and Content-Length logic as now. Non-200 statuses commit right away and need no snapshot.

Add a regression test for each: a hijack through httptest.NewServer using a raw net.Conn client, checking the status line, the header and the raw bytes; the server's `Config.ErrorLog` writing to a buffer, checking for no "hijacked" message; the late header change ignored the same way as plain net/http.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- The original criteria in /tmp/claude-0/-tmp-ff-eval-5q-zbnef-workspace/93253450-8e16-425a-95cc-77e1f0443814/scratchpad/ac.md still hold (read it).
- Hijack after a write produces the same bytes on the wire as plain net/http; Hijack with no write causes no server log and nothing written by finish.
- Headers changed after the 200 status was set are ignored, as in net/http.

CHECKS: while working: `go test -race ./middleware -run ETag`. At the end: `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (empty).
